title: Drought rain-slope loss held across 12 year starts at 158 south-east Australian catchments with two rain products
abstract: We tested whether the loss of annual runoff sensitivity to rain depends on the year boundary. We rebuilt daily CAMELS-AUS v2.03 records under all 12 month starts. One common set of 158 south-east Australian catchments passed the data rules for AGCD and SILO rain. Reference start labels were 1951-1995; test labels were 1997-2009 and 2010-2020. Separate linear fits used current and prior-year rain. Joint spatial and three-year block samples refitted both eras. In 1997-2009, current-rain slope losses were 31-37% with AGCD and 28-33% with SILO. All 12 approximate simultaneous 95% bands stayed below zero within each product. The sum of current- and prior-rain slopes also fell under all starts, so the loss did not simply move to the next-year term. Later point losses were 15-30% and 9-24%, but only four AGCD starts and no SILO starts had simultaneous bands below zero. Paired changes from January to July were uncertain. The year boundary does not remove the drought slope loss in this model and set. Short later eras, missing-flow adjustment, rain errors and model form limit the result. These are reused observations and fitted associations, not a physical cause or a test of the mean runoff deficit.
